subject.title: feat(memory): carry source actor context into recall

question: Should OpenClaw adopt `SourceActor` as an additive public plugin/memory supplement contract in this stack, or keep attribution private until a broader memory-tagging model is designed?
rationale: The code repair is mechanical, but the PR expands plugin SDK and memory supplement APIs that external plugins may rely on, so automation should not decide the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Adopt after fallback fix
options.body: Approve the additive contract after the missing `memory_get` fallback propagation is fixed and the stacked prerequisites are landed or rebased in order.

options.title: Keep private for now
options.body: Pause or close this PR and keep actor attribution internal until maintainers design a broader persisted-memory attribution model.

options.title: Split contract from memory behavior
options.body: Land the SourceActor channel/plugin contract first, then revisit memory supplement exposure in a narrower follow-up.

recommendation.title: Adopt after fallback fix
recommendation.body: Approve the additive contract after the missing `memory_get` fallback propagation is fixed and the stacked prerequisites are landed or rebased in order.

likelyOwner.reason: The history points to Peter Steinberger as the strongest owner across plugin SDK, memory host, and memory-core boundary decisions.
